_note: The pre-game and the post-game assessment (see autoload/assessment.gd). The same 12 scenario questions are asked before the first day and after the last one; their order and the order of the options are shuffled each time. Each question: id, topic (the threat or practice it checks), scenario, options (4), answer (the index of the best option, in this order). The assessment never says which answer is right. To change a question later, keep its id: the Google Sheet columns are the ids.
title: SECURITY CHECK

questions.scenario: At 3 a.m. an employee's account fails to sign in 20 times from another country, and then the next attempt works. The employee says they were asleep.
options: Nothing is wrong: the password was correct in the end.
Ask the employee to send you the password so you can check it.
Sign the account out, reset its password, turn on a second sign-in step, and review what the account touched.
Reset the password only, and leave the rest alone.

questions.scenario: A laptop has become very slow and strange windows keep opening. The user installed a free "PDF converter" from a website this morning.
options: Disconnect the laptop from the network, then scan it and remove the program before it is used again.
Close the windows and keep working.
Restart the laptop every day until the windows stop.
Install a second free cleaner program.

questions.scenario: Files on the shared drive are locked and a message demands payment. Last night's backup is stored offline and was not touched.
options: Pay quickly, so the files come back before the staff notice.
Delete the locked files and start the day's work again from nothing.
Restart every computer in the office at once.
Cut the affected computers off the network, remove the cause, then restore from the offline backup.

questions.scenario: A staff member who will leave next week starts copying project folders they have never used before.
options: Ignore it: they are a trusted employee.
Check what they can reach, keep only the access their job needs, and follow the company's process with HR and security.
Tell the whole team what you saw.
Give them administrator rights so everything they do is recorded.

questions.scenario: The logs show one workstation sending a large amount of data to an unknown server every night at the same hour. Nobody asked for this.
options: It is probably a system update. Do nothing.
Delete the old logs so the disk does not fill up.
Block that destination, isolate the workstation, and investigate what is leaving.
Give the workstation a faster internet line.

questions.scenario: A shop's website suddenly gets thousands of requests every second from many addresses. Real customers cannot open the pages.
options: Turn the firewall off so that more requests can get through.
Limit the rate of requests, filter the bad traffic, and add capacity or a protection service.
Ask the customers to refresh the page more often.
Block every address, including the customers'.

questions.scenario: An email from "it-supp0rt" says your password expires in one hour and gives a link to "confirm" it. The sender address does not match the company's.
options: Click the link to see where it goes, but do not type anything.
Do not click. Report the email, and check with IT through a way you already know.
Forward it to your coworkers so they can warn each other.
Reply and ask them to prove who they are.

questions.scenario: A login page puts what the visitor types straight into a database query. A visitor types ' OR '1'='1 as the password and gets in.
options: Ask users to choose longer passwords.
Hide the login page from search engines.
Make the text of the login form smaller.
Check the input and build the query with parameters, so typed text is never run as part of the query.

questions.scenario: A developer is about to upload code that has the database password written in it to a repository the whole team can read.
options: Keep secrets out of the code (use a secrets store or environment settings), and change the password that was exposed.
Upload it. The repository is private to the team.
Write the password in a comment so it is easy to find.
Upload it, and ask the team not to share it.

questions.scenario: A critical security fix is out for a library that the company website uses. It has not been tested with the site.
options: Never update: it works today.
Install it on the live site right now, with no backup.
Wait a year to see if other people have problems.
Back up the site, try the update on a copy first, and then apply it to the live site with a way to go back.

questions.scenario: A new intern only needs to read this month's sales report.
options: Give the intern the manager's account, so nothing needs to be set up.
Give read-only access to that report and nothing else.
Give access to every folder, in case it is needed later.
Make the intern an administrator: it is faster to set up.

questions.scenario: A company wants a backup plan that still works if ransomware locks everything on the network.
options: Keep one copy of the files on the same server.
Rely on the antivirus program and skip backups.
Keep several copies on different kinds of storage, with at least one offline or in another place, and test restoring them.
Keep a backup drive plugged into the server all the time.
